name: Question 17
problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ a \\ b \\ 5\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u⊥v$ and $u⊥w.$ What is the value of $a-b?$
worked_solution:
Given that $u⊥v$ and $u⊥w$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\cdot v=0 \\ u\cdot w=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's consider the first equation $u\cdot v=0.$ Calculating the dot product in terms of $a$ and $b$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ 2\cdot (-2)+a\cdot 1+b\cdot 5+5\cdot (-2) & =0 \\ -4+a+5b-10 & =0 \\ a+5b & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, for the second equation $u\cdot w=0$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & =0 \\ 2\cdot 1+a\cdot 4+b\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 1 & =0 \\ 2+4a-b+5 & =0 \\ 4a-b & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the values of $a$ and $b$, we need to solve the system

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}a+5b=14 \\ 4a-b=-7\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-4$ and adding the result to the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-21b=-63\,⟹\,b=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $b=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a+5(3) & =14 \\ a+15 & =14 \\ a & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have that

$$
a-b=-1-3=-4.
$$
